cards.text: Friend, this one starts quiet, so Papa's keeping his voice down for once. It's about Sarah, Abraham's wife, and the end of a long, long life.

cards.question: How old does Sarah, Abraham's wife, live to be?

cards.text: She dies in Kiriath-arba, that's Hebron, in the land of Canaan, and Abraham goes out to mourn and to weep for her. Then he gets up from beside her and goes to speak to the Hittites, the people living in that land.

cards.question: Abraham calls himself a foreigner and an outsider among the Hittites. He asks them to give him a ___ site among them.

cards.text: Abraham just called himself an outsider, and the Hittites answer him, “Listen to us, sir. You are God’s chosen one among us.” That's like introducing yourself as the new guy at work and finding out the whole office already knows your NAME.

cards.question: What do the Hittites offer Abraham so he can bury Sarah?

cards.text: Abraham rises, bows down before the Hittites, and asks them to go to Ephron son of Zohar for him. He's not browsing tombs, friend, he's got the address: the cave of Machpelah, at the end of Ephron's field.

cards.question: Abraham wants Ephron to sell him the cave of Machpelah right in front of everyone, for ___ price.

cards.text: Abraham's asking the Hittites to go talk to Ephron for him. Ephron? He's sitting RIGHT THERE among them at the gate of his city, with every Hittite listening.

cards.question: Abraham wants to buy the cave of Machpelah. With all the Hittites listening at the city gate, what does Ephron tell him about the cave?

answers.text: He gives it to Abraham as a gift
He offers a different cave instead

cards.question: Ephron gives Abraham the cave of Machpelah but keeps the field for himself.

cards.text: Again Abraham bows down before the people of the land, then turns to Ephron to give his answer. And the WHOLE city gate is leaning in like it's the last five seconds of a tied game.

cards.question: Abraham takes Ephron up on the gift of the field and the cave.
Ephron answers, “Listen to me, my lord.” He says the land is worth four hundred shekels of ___.

cards.text: Then Ephron adds, “but what is that between you and me? Bury your dead.” Friend, Mother Miller bought me for twenty-five cents, and Ephron's out here calling four hundred shekels NOTHING.

cards.question: Abraham talks Ephron down to a lower price.

cards.text: No haggling, no “is that your BEST price, my friend?” Abraham weighs out all four hundred shekels of silver, by the standard of the merchants, and Ephron's field at Machpelah near Mamre and the cave in it are deeded over to him in front of all the Hittites at the city gate.

cards.question: Besides Ephron's field and the cave of Machpelah, what else is deeded over to Abraham?

answers.text: All the trees in the field

cards.text: Then Abraham buries his wife Sarah in the cave of the field at Machpelah near Mamre, in the land of Canaan. The man who called himself a foreigner now has a field and a cave deeded to him as a burial site, and friend, Abraham's story isn't finished yet.
